close_reason: Both children closed: .9.1 (core check_shape API in pkix-lint, shipped commit 5c0d67de) and .9.2 (five per-profile convenience aliases, shipped commits e9c52dd8 + 472d27b4). The pkix-lint::check_shape convenience layer + per-profile shape-check aliases now exist as designed (single-cert structural sanity check sitting between pkix_path::validate_path and OSCAL Assessment Results output). 10 integration tests cross-validate the aliases against known-good and known-bad fixtures. All five aliases ship with the naming Mark approved 2026-05-12 (mirror Profile struct slug).
description:
## Why

Consumers regularly hold a single cert and want a fast Rust answer to "is this a sanely-shaped X cert?" — without running full path validation (no chain, maybe no anchors) and without OSCAL JSON output. Just `Result<(), Vec<Finding>>` in microseconds.

Use cases surfaced in conversation:

- TLS server logging client certs and pre-filtering noise.
- MTA classifying inbound S/MIME signatures.
- Operators triaging a cert dump.
- Pre-flight check before submitting a CSR for issuance.

This sits between `pkix-path::ValidationPolicy` (the path-validation gate concern) and OSCAL Assessment Results JSON (the compliance-assertion concern). It's a fast Rust convenience layer over the lint engine.

Closest ecosystem analog: zlint (Go, used by Let's Encrypt's issuance pipeline). It runs a per-purpose lint suite and emits structured findings. Slow per-cert because of its plugin architecture. A Rust equivalent that is in-process and OSCAL-aligned would be a real value-add.

## What

### Core API (in pkix-lint)

```rust
/// Run a profile's lints against a single cert.
/// Returns Ok if no Error/Fatal findings.
/// Returns Err with the findings list otherwise (may include Warn/Notice findings).
pub fn check_shape(cert: &Certificate, profile: &dyn LintProfile) -> Result<(), Vec<Finding>>;
```

The implementation iterates lints in the Profile's resolved Catalog and runs each against the cert. No chain walk, no signature verification, no I/O. O(number of lints in profile) where each lint is a structural check on parsed DER.

### Convenience aliases (in pkix-profiles)

```rust
/// RFC 5280 + RFC 6125 + serverAuth EKU — TLS server cert shape.
pub fn check_basic_tls_shape(cert: &Certificate) -> Result<(), Vec<Finding>>;

/// RFC 8551 §3 — S/MIME cert baseline shape.
pub fn check_basic_smime_shape(cert: &Certificate) -> Result<(), Vec<Finding>>;
```

### Convenience aliases (in pkix-profiles-cabf, reference / not authoritative)

```rust
/// CA/B Forum TLS BR shape (reference snapshot, not authoritative).
pub fn check_cabf_tls_br_shape(cert: &Certificate) -> Result<(), Vec<Finding>>;

/// CA/B Forum S/MIME BR Mailbox-validated shape (reference snapshot).
pub fn check_cabf_smime_br_shape(cert: &Certificate) -> Result<(), Vec<Finding>>;

/// CA/B Forum Code Signing BR shape (reference snapshot).
pub fn check_cabf_code_signing_shape(cert: &Certificate) -> Result<(), Vec<Finding>>;
```

Each alias is a one-liner calling `pkix_lint::check_shape(cert, &BasicTlsProfile)` etc.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pkix_lint::check_shape()` core API exists.
- [ ] `pkix_profiles::check_basic_tls_shape()` and `check_basic_smime_shape()` convenience aliases exist.
- [ ] `pkix-profiles-cabf` convenience aliases exist (depends on the crate existing per PKIX-amgn.2 + .4 having moved the Profile types in).
- [ ] Test vectors: known-good cert returns `Ok`; known-bad cert (e.g., missing serverAuth EKU for `check_basic_tls_shape`) returns `Err` with appropriate `Finding`s.
- [ ] Rustdoc clearly distinguishes shape-check (single cert, fast, structural) vs path-validation (chain, slow, full RFC 5280 §6) vs compliance-assertion (OSCAL Assessment Results, audit-trail).
- [ ] Performance smoke test: shape-check on a typical TLS cert runs in microseconds, not milliseconds. (Not a hard CI gate, just a sanity check.)

## Out of scope

- Path-validation concerns (those go through `pkix-path::validate_path`).
- OSCAL Assessment Results output (callers who want compliance vocabulary go through `pkix-lint`'s OSCAL serializer per PKIX-9vnx.3).
- Caching or memoization of repeated shape checks against the same cert.
- Async / streaming APIs.

## Depends on

- PKIX-9vnx.6 (Lint-as-Control mapping; needed so `check_shape()` can iterate registered lints from a Catalog by id).
- PKIX-amgn.4 (BasicTls / BasicSmime exist in pkix-profiles; CABF Profile types exist in pkix-profiles-cabf).

## Filed by

Surfaced in conversation 2026-05-11. Anchored by the per-rule-split stance PKIX-8qz1 ("Rust handles the executable side at every layer; OSCAL handles the policy-selection side") — this bead is the consumer-facing Rust convenience over the lint engine.
notes: Framing rework 2026-05-12 (PKIX-ncab.3, decision B): OSCAL is no longer the source of truth; it is one supported output format. The check_shape() API and per-profile aliases are independent of which output format consumers use for compliance reporting. .9.1 already shipped (commit 5c0d67de). User-facing docs in .9.x descendants should not present OSCAL as central. The 'OSCAL-aligned' phrasing in the rationale above is historical context, not a current goal. See memory pkix-oscal-demoted-2026-05-11.
title: pkix-lint: check_shape() convenience API + per-profile aliases
